title: Professor extra — Simple groups of orders 61 through 100
header:
Professor-supplied problem in the assignment; solution below is an internal derivation using Sylow theory and p-groups, without Feit–Thompson.

Prerequisites: @[Sylow theorem]cu:algebra:midterm-3:sylow:th:mt3-sylow; @[Unique, normal, and characteristic Sylow subgroups]cu:algebra:midterm-3:sylow:th:mt3-sylow-normality; @[Counting distinct prime-order subgroups]cu:algebra:midterm-3:sylow:th:mt3-prime-order-intersections; @[Faithful actions of simple groups and the alternating-group obstruction]cu:algebra:midterm-3:foundations:th:mt3-simple-actions; @[Every index-two subgroup is normal]cu:algebra:midterm-3:foundations:th:mt3-index-two; @[A nontrivial finite p-group has nontrivial center]cu:algebra:midterm-3:sylow:th:mt3-pgroups; @[Groups of order p² are abelian]cu:algebra:midterm-3:sylow:th:mt3-p-square-abelian; @[Abelian simple groups have prime order]cu:algebra:midterm-3:foundations:th:mt3-abelian-simple; @[Normalizer]cu:algebra:midterm-3:foundations:df:mt3-normalizer; @[Lagrange’s theorem and the index formula]cu:algebra:midterm-3:foundations:th:mt3-lagrange.
